title: Capacity signal convergence and staggered priming to prevent GPU queue spirals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a hosted API capacity event on 2025-02-10 we observed a sustained GPU pool exhaustion that manifested as long tail queue growth, aggressive throttling, and repeated partial evictions. This ticket consolidates follow-ups from the postmortem and defines an action plan focused on aligning capacity signals, reducing feedback amplification, and introducing a staggered priming strategy that trades a small steady cost for much lower risk of spiral queue growth.

Root cause (short):
- Multiple reactive signals (queue length, CPU pressure, and utilization) independently triggered scale-up/down actions and eviction heuristics with differing time windows.
- Autoscaler prewarm was binary (cold/hot) and attempted large-scale priming simultaneously across multiple pools, causing temporary oversubscription and contention for GPU memory/KV cache.
- Admission controller used a reactive instantaneous threshold which allowed rapid enqueues during scale operations, amplifying the queue backlog when capacity briefly dipped.

Goals for this ticket:
1) Define and implement a "convergence" layer that aggregates multiple telemetry signals into a single stable scaling decision (signal smoothing + weighted consensus).
2) Implement staggered priming where prewarm is spread across sub-pools based on a deterministic jitter to avoid simultaneous large memory pressure events.
3) Harden admission control with short-term admission smoothing (token-bucket + exponentially weighted moving average) and a capped fast-fail path for enormous bursts.
4) Create a rollout plan, monitoring/alerting, and a post-rollout validation checklist.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Signal convergence: create an autoscaler algorithm that computes a composite score from queue-ms, GPU-util-1m, cache-miss-rate, and SLO-violation-rate. Use a 60s window for smoothing and a configurable hysteresis percentage for scale down.
- Staggered priming: when the autoscaler decides to prime N GPUs, assign priming start times using deterministic jitter across 30-90s window by pool shard. Priming throttles KV-cache prefetch and warm-start slot allocation to keep memory pressure below threshold.
- Admission smoothing: replace the current instantaneous admission threshold with a short token-bucket that refills based on observed service time distribution and conservatively estimates free slots. Add a capped fast-fail policy (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) for requests that exceed a burst budget to avoid queue amplification.
- Cost control: instrument a "priming budget" per customer tier to limit cost from prewarming; accept trade-off of modest priming cost for improved tail latency and stability.

Action items (concrete):
- ENG-783412-A: Design spec for signal convergence algorithm (owner: Jonah) — due 2025-02-21.
- ENG-783412-B: Implement convergence aggregator and expose composite score in autoscaler telemetry (owner: Priya Rao) — due 2025-02-28.
- ENG-783412-C: Implement deterministic jitter priming scheduler + memory-pressure guard (owner: Marco Li) — due 2025-03-05.
- ENG-783412-D: Replace admission threshold with token-bucket + fast-fail hook, add metrics for dropped/fast-failed requests (owner: Jonah) — due 2025-03-07.
- ENG-783412-E: Create runbook and rollback procedure for the rollout (owner: SRE oncall lead) — due 2025-03-09.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No queue-length spikes > 10x baseline during scale events in synthetic stress tests modeled after the Feb-10 incident.
- 95th percentile latency improves by at least 30% vs current behavior during transient capacity reductions.
- Number of tenant-impacting 5xx/429 incidents attributable to capacity events reduced by 80% in the first 7 days post-rollout.
- Priming cost delta capped at < 7% of baseline serving costs for medium-tier customers.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Staggered priming increases short-term cumulative GPU usage compared to zero-priming, but reduces the probability of cache thrash and queue amplification which causes higher customer-visible failures and retries (more expensive overall).
- Signal convergence reduces noisy scale churn but adds complexity to autoscaler logic and requires thorough telemetry coverage to avoid blind spots.
- Admission smoothing introduces an artificial limiter that can increase visible 429s for very large bursts; the plan includes a clear communication strategy and a retry/backoff header to make client behavior graceful.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Feature flags behind a runtime gate: convergence-only (no priming), convergence+staggered-priming in small pools (non-critical tenants), admission smoothing enabled in canary route.
2) 48h canary followed by a 7d progressive ramp across pools with automated rollback triggers on increased SLO violations.
3) Post-rollout validation runbook to run synthetic traffic profiles and compare telemetry against acceptance criteria.

Monitoring and alerts to add:
- Composite score time-series + alert when score crosses scale-threshold but no scale occurs in 90s.
- Priming memory pressure gauge per pool shard with alert on > 85% reserved-memory during priming window.
- Admission smooth drop rate and fast-fail rate with a P50/P95 latency of accepted vs failed requests.

Notes and links:
- Full incident postmortem: https://docs.internal.redwood.com/postmortems/2025-02-10-gpu-capacity-exhaustion (private)
- Initial convergence design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/11234 (WIP)
- Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-runbook-drafts (internal)

Owner responsibilities and next steps:
- Jonah to finish the design doc and coordinate with Priya/Marco for telemetry requirements.
- SRE will prepare canary pools and ensure rollback automation is in place before any priming rollout.
- Product/Support to prepare customer-facing comms template for expected Retry-After behavior in the first wave.

This ticket will track design, implementation, rollout, and validation for the convergence + staggered-priming approach. If this proves insufficient, follow-ups will investigate KV-cache eviction policy changes and a finer-grained per-tenant allocation circuit breaker.
